name: Immigration and paralegal services

pf.license.what the business is (a switch set at si: 1) A document preparer or immigration consultant who is not a lawyer (the example business): fills in forms only from the customer's own answers, translates, and mails what the customer signed; never gives legal advice, never picks a form, never represents anyone before the immigration agencies. 2) A law firm: legal advice by its lawyers. 3) A recognized nonprofit with accredited representatives: legal advice by those representatives.
pf.license.need: Non-lawyer: a business registration, plus an immigration consultant registration and a bond where the state's rules require them. Law firm: each lawyer's active license in good standing in any state (immigration is federal law), plus the state's rules for law firms. Nonprofit: the organization's federal recognition and each representative's current federal accreditation (the federal rule: only a lawyer or an accredited representative of a recognized organization may give immigration legal advice or represent someone).
pf.license.ask: The registration number and bond where the state form asks; for a law firm each lawyer's bar number; for a nonprofit its recognition and each representative's accreditation and end date.
pf.license.who holds it: The business (registration, bond); each lawyer; each accredited representative.
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, registration, accreditation or bond (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: nothing waits on a license or registration (D96): the business goes live once set up and the owner says yes. A business that says it is a law firm or a recognized nonprofit lists legal consultations; any other business lists only form help at the customer's direction and translation. A job the owner says needs a registration they don't have isn't booked.
pf.license.renewals: The owner may give end dates for a registration, bond or accreditation; Rosie reminds Sam before they pass and pauses new bookings for that work if the owner says it lapsed. It looks nothing up.
pf.license.insurance or bond: A bond in the amount the state's rules set, where they require one, and errors and omissions insurance, are the business's own; Rosie shows them only as the business gives them.

pf.services.shape: Consult: appointments to fill in immigration forms from the customer's own answers, certified translation of documents, and (only where the business has a lawyer or an accredited representative) legal consultations. The case, the filing and any agency appointment stay outside Rosie.
pf.services.examples: The example business's own prices, not a standard.

pf.questions.who may book: An adult books for themselves. A family member may book for a parent or a relative who can't, but the person the forms are for gives their own answers on their own secure page and signs their own forms. A child's forms: a parent or legal guardian books and signs.

stop.words: someone is in danger or being hurt right now, or a medical emergency

goOn.words: an immigration arrest or detention happening now, or a relative just detained
goOn.what: not 911 unless someone is in danger. A non-lawyer business says plainly it can't help with a detention or a court case, and that an immigration lawyer or an accredited representative can (the federal government lists accredited representatives; the state bar runs a lawyer referral line), naming nobody. A law firm gives its own urgent line.

goOn.words: abuse, or fear of a partner or family member
goOn.what: if in danger, 911; the National Domestic Violence Hotline, 1-800-799-7233; the booking goes on, and Rosie asks how it's safe to reach the customer

goOn.words: a notice with a deadline in days, or a hearing notice
goOn.what: the date is put on the booking for the owner, and only times before it are offered; a non-lawyer business tells the customer plainly that a lawyer or an accredited representative should see a hearing notice

pf.safety.never said: No promise of a result or a faster answer, and no claim of ties to the government.

pf.first_steps.documents: The plug-in's list per form package (the notice, the current card, the passport page, prior forms), uploaded on the secure page or brought as copies. Originals are looked at and handed back the same visit.
pf.first_steps.prep for the reminder: Bring every notice you got from the government, a photo ID, and the documents on your list. Originals are handed back.

pf.visit.check-in: At the office: the code at the front desk. By video: the preparer asks for the code at the start. At a forms day: the code at the host's table. At home: the code at the door.
pf.visit.at the visit: The preparer types the forms from the customer's own answers, reads every answer back in the customer's language, and the customer signs. The preparer signs as the preparer where the form asks. Copies go to the customer; originals are handed back.
pf.visit.work changes: An extra form is priced and OK'd before it's typed. A question that needs legal advice stops that part: the business can't advise, and nothing is charged for it.
pf.visit.what proves it's done: DONE once the forms are signed and the copies given. If the customer asks the business to mail them, the tracking number goes on the secure page.
pf.visit.translation: A copy is dropped off with the code, or uploaded. READY when the certified translation is done: on the secure page, or picked up with the code.

pf.money.before: Forms appointments: nothing taken (the starting answer). Translation: paid in full at drop-off or upload. A home appointment may save a card for the travel-fee amount the business sets as its late-cancel or no-show fee. Where the state's rules require a written contract before any money, nothing is taken until it's signed. A deposit only where the state's rules allow it, up to the state's cap.
pf.money.after: Paid at the front desk when the forms are signed; by video or at home, the bill is texted, or a saved card is charged at DONE. An extra form is priced and OK'd first, and paid with the rest at the visit.
pf.money.government fees: Never through Rosie: the customer pays the government directly, the agency's own way. The business never holds them.
pf.money.fees: No late-cancel or no-show fee by default. A business may set one (the example: the $40 travel fee at a home visit); it's shown before booking, and Sam confirms each. A fee is never more than what was paid now.
pf.money.tax: None by default; where the state's rules tax the service, the rate comes from the state form.
pf.money.rosfield: the $2 per confirmed booking applies, as to every kind of work (D97): a flat fee for each booking Rosie's AI makes, paid by the business, never added to the customer's price; a booking the business puts in itself carries no $2; card payments cost only Stripe's own card fee.
pf.money.law firm switch: A law firm or a nonprofit: money paid before legal work is an advance fee for the firm's trust account, never through Rosie, so legal consultations take nothing before. Its translation and form help follow the lines above.

pf.messages.texts say: only the business's plain name, the date, the time and the place; the owner may set a plain display name for texts and card statements
pf.messages.staff texts: initials and 'forms appointment', never the form type or status
pf.messages.others asking: Rosie never confirms to anyone but the customer that a person is a customer or has a booking: not a relative, an employer or an officer. A request from law enforcement goes to the owner.
pf.messages.safe to text: If texts aren't safe, only the way the customer picks.
pf.messages.languages: English and Spanish, plus any languages the owner adds (often Chinese, Vietnamese, Tagalog, Haitian Creole, Arabic, Portuguese); any required notice in the customer's language.
pf.messages.minors: A parent or legal guardian books; texts go to them.
pf.messages.no nudges: No follow-up texts selling more forms.

pf.staff.roles: Document preparers (not lawyers), translators, an office manager. At a law firm: lawyers and paralegals working under them. At a nonprofit: accredited representatives.
pf.staff.licenses: No person license at the example business. Translators certify their own translations. Lawyers and accredited representatives, where the business has them, are listed as the business gives them; Rosie doesn't look them up or check them.
pf.staff.supervision: A non-lawyer never gives legal advice, never picks a form, never represents anyone. A paralegal at a law firm works under a lawyer.
pf.staff.skills: languages spoken; form packages; translation language pairs
pf.staff.who OKs: Sam OKs any deadline request and any price made for one customer.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Another preparer who speaks the customer's language. A customer who asked for a person by name is asked first, and nobody moves on silence.

pf.rules.legal advice: Only a lawyer or an accredited representative of a recognized organization gives immigration legal advice (the federal rule, as a switch). Rosie never gives legal advice. Everyone else fills in forms only from the customer's own answers.
pf.rules.words never used: Never call the business or anyone in it a lawyer, an attorney, 'notario' or 'notario público', or an immigration expert, unless that is true. No promises of results or speed; no claim of ties to the government.
pf.rules.notice: Where the state's rules require it: a notice that the business isn't a lawyer and can't give legal advice, in English and the customer's language, shown at booking and posted at the office. Rosie shows it as the business gives it.
pf.rules.written contract: Before paid services where the state's rules require it, with the state's cancel period and a full refund inside it.
pf.rules.originals: Never kept; copies of everything filed go to the customer.
pf.rules.government fees: Separate, paid by the customer to the government.
pf.rules.records: 7 years, or longer where the state's rules for consultants require it. The forms themselves stay in the business's own files.
pf.rules.no referral fees: The business never pays or takes a fee for sending someone to a lawyer.

matter most.a legal question at a non-lawyer busines: Never answered; the business can't advise; only form help the customer directs is booked.
matter most.a deadline in days: Sam's OK first; only times before the date; if nothing fits, said plainly.
matter most.a relative books for someone detained: A non-lawyer business can't help with detention; a law firm's own urgent line.
matter most.texts aren't safe: Only the way the customer picks.
matter most.the forms need a lawyer (a past removal,: That part stops at the visit; nothing is charged for it.
matter most.a no-show: No fee unless the business set one and the customer agreed.

pf.edges.the rest: All other edge cases are handled the generic way.

Built Tue Oct 27 2026 (REDESIGN 2 master, N3b) from the lawyer overlay ("from": "lawyer") merged with the verified test-drive plug-in (immigration-services, Oct 25: its pf.* text, services, prices and rules kept; the backup is in the batch scratch folder). Rosie never gives legal advice and never checks a license, registration, accreditation or bond (D96): pf.license says so.
Prices (the example business's own, from the verified plug-in): forms appointment $150 a form package; extra form $60; certified translation $35 a page ($105 for 3 pages, paid in full); a home appointment $190 = $150 + the $40 travel fee (one price, so the bill adds up). The $40 travel fee is also the late-cancel / no-show fee on the one card path (a card saved, charged at DONE). Government filing fees never go through Rosie.
